title: Parents' attitudes and funeral bands near Newcomb
summary: Friends loved jazz but parents disliked it; she recalls funeral bands playing dirges then jazz near Newcomb in 1922.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, do you remember what your parents and your friends' parents thought about it, and what your friends thought about it when it first started, you know, having any work, it first started becoming acceptable? Well... Good Society in New Orleans, have it played a part in David Dorn part in the best life?

It was, Pierron was already established that the country club for us came there, so I don't know, it was before my time that he started playing there. And all of my friends loved it. Their parents didn't care for it too much. But, uh, I remember when I was at Newcomb, uh, that was in 1922, I guess. They, um, uh, there was a Negro, uh, sanitary near Newcomb. And, um, they would, uh, always have a band, you know, going, uh, preceding the funeral procession. And they'd play very slow duages going to the cemetery. And then coming back, they'd really break out and play wonderful jazz. We used to be, you know, sitting out on the campus sometimes, studying, and we'd hear them just really going to town, or going home from the funeral. But, um, as I say, there are several others that know a whole lot more about it, the early start, because it was fairly well established by the time I made my debut.
